lines.text: In wound healing, which cells are responsible for wound contraction?
Meet the purple fibroblasts. Each one grabs a rope tied across the wound.
Together they pull hard from both sides. This is wound contraction.
(laugh) The two smiling wound edges are drawn together, and the gap closes.
Macrophages have another job. They engulf foreign matter by phagocytosis and release cytokines for inflammation and healing.
Reticulocytes are immature red blood cells, with no real role in wound contraction.
Remember: in wound contraction, fibroblasts pull the two wound edges together.
Which is a feature of an adenoma?
Here is a calm adenoma, a benign tumour, resting on its red cushion.
It sits inside a clear bubble. Adenomas are typically encapsulated.
(sigh) Look at the squashed cells below. As it grows slowly, it compresses the normal tissue around it.
That compressed tissue forms a pseudocapsule.
Some cells may be dysplastic, but they cannot invade the basement membrane or metastasize, so it is still benign.
Dysplasia is a step toward malignancy, and severe dysplasia is the same as carcinoma in situ.
Remember: an adenoma is a slow-growing, benign tumour, typically encapsulated.
